EXPLANATION: The spectrum is characteristic of a para-disubstituted benzene: a very intense ring–breathing Raman line at 998 cm⁻¹ and the para CH wag near 847 cm⁻¹. 670 cm⁻¹ is typical for an aryl C–Cl stretch, indicating a chlorine substituent on the ring. Bands at 1071, 1167 and 1204 cm⁻¹ fit C–O and C–S stretches of a methoxy-thioether group, while 1458 cm⁻¹ corresponds to CH₃ deformation and 1572/1600 cm⁻¹ to the usual aromatic ring ν(CC). Among the candidates only molecule 2 (COCSc1ccc(Cl)cc1) is a para-chlorophenyl bearing both methoxy (–OCH₃) and thioether (–S–) groups, matching all key features, whereas the other candidates lack either the Cl (no 670/510 cm⁻¹) or the correct substitution pattern.
